properties.areaDesc: Aiken, SC; Lexington, SC; Saluda, SC
properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 10 at 7:02PM EDT until October 10 at 7:30PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
TORCAE

The National Weather Service in Columbia has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northwestern Lexington County in central South Carolina...
Eastern Saluda County in central South Carolina...
North central Aiken County in central South Carolina...

* Until 730 PM EDT.

* At 702 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Ridge Spring, or near Batesburg-Leesville, moving
north at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Batesburg-Leesville around 705 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Cedar
Grove Fire Station, South Shore Marina, Oswald Park, Fredonia, Siesta
Cove Marina, Wyses Ferry, Monetta, Lake Murray Shores, Circle Fire
Station, and Hollow Creek Public Park.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to an interior room or closet on the lowest floor of a
sturdy building immediately.

This Tornado Warning includes portions of Lake Murray. Boaters, move
to shore and take shelter on the lowest floor of the closest sturdy
building!

CMAMtext: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 7:30 PM EDT. Take shelter now. Check media.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 7:30 PM EDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

properties.areaDesc: Aiken, SC; Edgefield, SC; Lexington, SC; Saluda, SC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 7:00PM EDT until October 10 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
FFWCAE

The National Weather Service in Columbia has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Aiken County in central South Carolina...
East Central Edgefield County in central South Carolina...
West Central Lexington County in central South Carolina...
Eastern Saluda County in central South Carolina...

* Until 1000 PM EDT.

* At 700 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Batesburg-Leesville, Ridge Spring, Summit, Monetta, Ward, Hibernia,
Kneece, Fredonia, Delmar, Circle Fire Station, Murray, Cedar Grove
Fire Station, South Shore Marina, Riverbend Boat Ramp, Lake Murray
Shores, Hollow Creek Public Park, Oswald Park, Siesta Cove Marina
and Shull Island.

This includes Interstate 20 in South Carolina between mile markers 24
and 32.
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 6:51PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
At 651 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Hawthorne, or 9 miles north of Citra, moving north at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts around 40 mph and minor flooding due to heavy
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor flooding due to heavy rainfall is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Interlachen, Keystone Heights, Melrose, Citra, Hawthorne, George's
Lake, Lake Geneva, Florahome, Melrose Landing, and Cross Creek.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego, CA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 3:26PM PDT until October 11 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in San Diego has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in California...

San Diego River At Fashion Valley affecting San Diego County.

.Widespread moderate to locally heavy rainfall associated with
Tropical Storm Rachel over the San Diego River basin is expected
tonight into late Sunday morning. The San Diego River at Fashion
Valley is expected to peak at 8.1 ft (action/monitor stage) just
before Noon on Sunday, falling below action stage Sunday afternoon.

For the San Diego River...including Fashion Valley...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Diego River at Fashion Valley.

* WHEN...For Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.5 feet, Action stage. The first real impacts are
seen on the San Diego River at this level. Low lying roads in and
around Fashion Valley Mall begin to take on water. Avenida Del Rio
is the first road to begin flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM PDT Saturday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
late tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 7.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1000 AM PDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SUNDAY AFTERNOON
